title: A habit tracker
description:
Build the tested core of the habit tracker from lesson 6.05, in TypeScript. With it, the app's `main.ts` only has to wire events to `dispatch`. Dates are `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings. ```typescript interface Habit { id: number; name: string; days: string[] } // days ticked, sorted, no repeats interface State { version: 2; habits: Habit[]; nextId: number } type Action = | { type: "add"; name: string } | { type: "rename"; id: number; name: string } | { type: "toggle"; id: number; day: string } | { type: "remove"; id: number }; const initialState: State // { version: 2, habits: [], nextId: 1 } function update(state: State, action: Action): State function streak(days: readonly string[], today: string): number function render(state: State, today: string): string function load(storage: StorageLike): State function save(storage: StorageLike, state: State): boolean ``` where `StorageLike` is `{ getItem(key: string): string | null; setItem(key: string, value: string): void }`. **update** never changes the state it is given. When an action changes nothing, it returns the **same** state object. - `add`: trims the name. An empty name, or one that matches an existing habit's name ignoring case, changes nothing. Otherwise adds `{ id: nextId, name, days: [] }` and increases `nextId`. - `rename`: the same name rules (the habit's own current name does not count as a clash); an unknown id changes nothing. - `toggle`: adds the day if it is not ticked, removes it if it is; `days` stays sorted. An unknown id changes nothing. - `remove`: an unknown id changes nothing. **streak** counts consecutive ticked days ending **today**; if today is not ticked yet, ending **yesterday** (so a streak is not lost before the day is over). Otherwise 0. Work with UTC dates: `Date.UTC` or `new Date(day + "T00:00:00Z")`. **render** returns HTML on one line, with every name escaped (`& < > " '`): - no habits: `

No habits yet.

` - otherwise `
    `, then for each habit in order `
  • N days
    • ` with `aria-pressed` telling whether today is ticked and `1 day` for a streak of 1, then `

D of T done today

`. **load** reads the key `"habits"`: - a version 2 state is used if it has the right shape (a `habits` array of objects with a number `id`, a string `name` and a `days` array of strings, and a number `nextId`); its days are sorted and repeats removed; - **version 1** was `{ "version": 1, "habits": [{ "name": ..., "done": [...] }] }`: give the habits ids 1, 2, 3... in order, use `done` as `days`, and set `nextId` after them; - anything else (missing, corrupt JSON, wrong shape, unknown version, a throwing `getItem`): `initialState`. **save** writes the state as JSON under `"habits"` and returns `true`, or `false` if `setItem` throws.
hints: Go one function at a time: `update` first (it is used by the other tests), then `streak`, `render`, and finally `load`.

For `streak`, step back one day at a time with `t -= 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` on UTC times and turn each back into `YYYY-MM-DD` with `new Date(t).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`. UTC days are always 24 hours long, so month ends and leap years just work.
In `load`, write a type guard `isHabit(x: unknown): x is Habit` and check every part of the stored object before building a `State` from it.
requirements: The `Action` type as a discriminated union, handled with an exhaustive `switch`.
`update`, `streak` and `render` are pure: no storage, no clock (`today` is passed in), no DOM.
Stored data is treated as `unknown` and checked before use.
stretch: Write the `main.ts` from lesson 6.05 around these functions and open it in a real browser with Vite.
rules: Make the switch in update exhaustive with a never check.
Treat stored data as unknown before checking it.
Use the storage passed in, not localStorage directly.
Keep the functions pure: today is passed in, so do not read the clock.
